raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not like to change too much. What worked on my land before, I mostly keep doing. On my 6 mu, I will still keep wheat-maize on most of the land because that is the safest way to have grain and cash, and I will keep a little cotton because I have grown it many years and know how to manage it. Family labor is not as full as before because some people work outside, so I cannot make a plan that needs too much hand work or too many trips to the field.

For this year, I would put about 4 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and 2 mu into cotton. Wheat I sow in October with the local habit, not too early, not too late. I usually use a common local wheat seed, maybe the same dealer as the neighbors. I still put fertilizer, because if wheat is hungry the yield falls badly, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. But I cannot spend too much, so I do a moderate amount, with most before sowing and one topdress later if the crop looks weak. After wheat harvest, maize must go in fast. That turnaround is always tight, so I keep tillage simple and use the usual way. For maize I use hybrid seed because local people around here mostly do that and it gives steadier yield. Cotton I keep on 2 mu only. Cotton takes more watching and more picking, so I do not want too much at my age. I will fertilize it, but not heavily, and irrigate only when it is really needed because pumping water costs money.
